title: McGeary's Pub
venue_description:
McGeary's Pub

McGeary's Pub is an Irish pub on Clinton Square in downtown Albany, long established as one of the city's most reliable live music venues, with a proper stage and sound system that punches above what most neighborhood pubs offer.

Atmosphere and Setting

The pub has a classic Irish-bar feel with a genuine music-venue backbone, drawing a mix of downtown Albany regulars and touring-band audiences depending on the night.

CRBN Blues Jam

Every Sunday night at 7:30 PM, the Capital Region Blues Network hosts its weekly blues jam — billed as “the coolest jam in the Capital Region.” A host band plays a one-hour opening set, after which the jam master organizes sign-up musicians into groups by instrument and musical compatibility, giving each a three-song set. McGeary's supplies a full backline, including a drum kit, bass amp, two guitar amps and a complete PA system, so musicians need only bring their own instrument.

Other Programming

Beyond the Sunday blues jam, McGeary's books a steady lineup of local and touring bands throughout the week.

For Performers

A sign-up sheet is typically placed on the first table inside the door; arriving early is recommended to secure a slot given the jam's popularity. There's no cover charge, though a $5 donation is suggested to support the host band.

Good to Know

McGeary's Pub is located at 4 Clinton Square, Albany, NY 12207. Children under 18 must be accompanied by an adult, and alcohol service is restricted to guests 21 and older.

title: The Lark Street Tavern
venue_description:
The Lark Street Tavern

The Lark Street Tavern is a neighborhood bar on Madison Avenue in Albany's Center Square/Lark Street district, an area long known as the heart of the city's bar and restaurant scene.

Atmosphere and Setting

The tavern has built a reputation around its sound quality — the venue itself describes its open mic as “the best sounding open mic in the area” — and draws a loyal following of neighborhood regulars alongside newcomers looking for a solid acoustic room.

Open Mic Night

Every Wednesday night, with sign-up beginning at 6:30 PM, the tavern welcomes musicians, poets and speakers of all kinds to its stage for a relaxed, community-driven open mic.

Other Programming

The Lark Street Tavern also hosts scheduled live jazz performances and other genre nights, contributing to Albany's broader downtown live-music calendar.

For Performers

Because the room is known for its sound, it's a good option for performers who want their set to actually sound good rather than just be heard.

Good to Know

The Lark Street Tavern is located at 453 Madison Ave, Albany, NY 12210, in the Lark Street entertainment district.

title: September's Too
venue_description:
September's Too

September's Too is a neighborhood tavern and sports bar on Central Avenue in Albany, with an outdoor patio featuring a gazebo, firepits and cornhole alongside a full indoor bar and stage area.

Atmosphere and Setting

The bar leans into a casual sports-bar identity most nights, with televisions and bar food, but its performance nights bring in a dedicated crowd of local musicians and regulars.

The Premier Open Mic

Every Thursday night at 8:00 PM, host Cool Universe runs The Premier Open Mic, a structured show that opens with a 10-minute set followed by a 17-minute featured artist performance before the open list begins. Each performer on the open list gets two songs or 10 minutes, whichever comes first, and backline is provided for all musicians, singers and artists.

Other Programming

September's Too also runs karaoke nights, other live music bookings and food specials such as 25-cent wing days throughout the week.

For Performers

Because backline is provided and the format is clearly structured, it's an approachable room for musicians who don't want to haul their own gear.

Good to Know

September's Too is located at 1165 Central Ave, Albany, NY 12205.

title: Caffe Lena
venue_description:
Caffè Lena

Caffè Lena is a legendary folk music listening room in downtown Saratoga Springs, about a 30-minute drive north of Albany, and one of the oldest continuously operating folk venues in the United States. Since opening in 1960, it has hosted a who's-who of folk and Americana artists early in their careers, and it remains a nonprofit dedicated to acoustic music.

Atmosphere and Setting

The room is intimate and reverent — a true listening room where audiences come to actually pay attention, in contrast to the background-music feel of many bar venues. That atmosphere carries over into its community jam nights as much as its ticketed concerts.

Bluegrass Jam

On select Wednesday evenings from 7:00 PM to 9:00 PM, Caffè Lena hosts a Bluegrass Jam open to all — players and listeners alike are invited to join the circle for classic bluegrass, newgrass and folk favorites. The group Red Spruce typically opens with a few tunes before the circle takes over, with musicians leading songs and others providing backup. Newcomers are encouraged to bring simple, prepared tunes to keep the circle moving.

Other Programming

Caffè Lena's regular calendar features touring folk, Americana and singer-songwriter acts, along with its own open mic nights and songwriter showcases.

For Performers

The bluegrass jam is a welcoming, informal circle rather than a stage show, making it approachable for pickers of varying skill levels who want to play traditional tunes in a listening-room setting.

Good to Know

Caffè Lena is located at 47 Phila Street, Saratoga Springs, NY 12866, about a 30-minute drive from downtown Albany. A $5 donation at the door is requested.
